edges.effect_quant: A 2022 network meta-analysis of 13 randomized trials and 944 patients found the low-FODMAP diet ranked first for global IBS symptom improvement, with a relative risk of symptoms not improving of 0.67 versus habitual diet. A 2021 meta-analysis found a moderate-to-large reduction in IBS severity with an SMD of -0.66.
edges.population: adults with irritable bowel syndrome using a short-term structured low-FODMAP diet
edges.mechanism: Short-term FODMAP restriction lowers the osmotic load and fermentable substrate burden in the gut, which can reduce distension, gas-related discomfort, and symptom flares in sensitive IBS patients.
edges.summary: This is one of the most consistent non-drug IBS interventions in the literature. Short-term low-FODMAP protocols repeatedly outperform habitual diet or sham-style comparators for global symptoms, even though they are not meant to be followed in the strict elimination phase forever.
edges.caveats: The intervention works best when it is structured and time-limited, and the long-term microbiome tradeoffs matter. The strict elimination phase should ideally be followed by reintroduction and personalization rather than indefinite maximal restriction.

evidence.notes: Efficacy of a low FODMAP diet in irritable bowel syndrome: systematic review and network meta-analysis.
